source_records.source_title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
source_records.author_or_publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union / EUR-Lex
source_records.system_or_product: EU Artificial Intelligence Act regulatory framework
source_records.deployment_context: Regulation of high-risk AI systems and general-purpose AI models in the European Union.
source_records.source_context: Articles 21, 73 to 78 and 91 to 92 recognise reasoned competent-authority requests for information and logs, serious-incident reporting, provider investigation and cooperation, preservation against incident-cause impairment, market-surveillance and fundamental-rights authority access, confidential handling, Commission information requests, independent experts and technical evaluation access. Article 78 requires protection of intellectual property, confidential business information and trade secrets, investigation and audit integrity, security interests, proceedings and classified information; it also limits collection to strictly necessary data and requires cybersecurity and deletion controls.
source_records.relevance_note: Authoritative regulatory basis showing that necessary authority access, provider cooperation, incident reporting, cause-preserving investigation and confidentiality safeguards are complementary requirements rather than alternatives.

primary_artefact_access.reviewing_system: OpenAI ChatGPT — GitHub-connected Codex work mode
primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of the official EUR-Lex text and article-level retrieval.
limitations: This source establishes EU legal requirements and a normative comparator; the record does not claim that the EU AI Act governs CAM or every AI system globally.
The record does not treat the Act, a regulatory request or a legal duty as an incident.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used as authoritative evidence that competent-authority access, serious-incident reporting, evidence-preserving investigation, provider cooperation, proportionality and confidentiality protections are recognised governance requirements.

source_records.source_title: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 on market surveillance and compliance of products
source_records.author_or_publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union / EUR-Lex
source_records.system_or_product: EU market-surveillance framework incorporated by the AI Act
source_records.deployment_context: Market surveillance, investigation and enforcement powers applied to AI systems through Article 74 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
source_records.source_context: Article 14 requires proportionate market-surveillance, investigation and enforcement powers, including powers to require relevant documents, technical specifications, data and compliance information; obtain copies; inspect premises; initiate investigations; access embedded software where necessary; and use information, documents, findings, statements or intelligence as evidence.
source_records.relevance_note: Authoritative external basis for a reasoned, necessary and proportionate evidence-access pathway capable of supporting an actual compliance investigation rather than disclosure in the abstract.

primary_artefact_access.reviewing_system: OpenAI ChatGPT — GitHub-connected Codex work mode
primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of the official EUR-Lex text, including Article 14.
limitations: This source concerns powers conferred under EU and national law; CAM cannot create or expand those legal powers.
Its use is limited to demonstrating the governance function and bounded character of investigative access.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to establish that investigation powers may include necessary access to technical evidence while remaining subject to proportionality, procedural safeguards and data-protection law.

source_records.source_title: Caelestis regulatory-interface, incident-response, audit, assurance, security and arbitration coverage review
source_records.deployment_context: Current Caelestis working branch governance/social-advice-calibration at commit aaae4c4524748970d88c1ef93a562392dd4a1c07.
source_records.source_context: Clause-level review covered OPERATIONS-003 incident lifecycle and evidence preservation; OPERATIONS-004 reporting, regulatory routing, retention and disclosure handling; OPERATIONS-001-SUP-01 evidentiary integrity, audit triggers, incident records, lawful oversight and archival reconstruction; OPERATIONS-008 external evaluators and adversarial-evaluation incident reporting; SECURITY-001 and SECURITY-002 boundary, privacy, authorised-inspection and sovereign-assurance controls; STEWARD-003 auditability, non-refusal and neutrality assurance; OPERATIONS-002 and AEON-005 arbitration evidence and confidentiality; and AEON-003-SCH-04 access-state non-authority. The review found strong adjacent controls but no general authority-verification, request, production, controlled-inspection, withholding-review and access-audit pathway for serious-incident, compliance, causal or remediation evidence.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary internal evidence for partial corpus coverage and the remaining structural pathway gap.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct recursive repository search followed by clause-level review of source-authoritative and adjacent instruments on the current working branch.
limitations: The assessment establishes corpus coverage, not implementation by an external provider or regulator.
No Caelestis amendment was drafted or adopted in this review.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to verify that the apparent gap is substantive rather than a first-search, naming or locality error.
